note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 7603 / 出力 10322 トークン

data.assessment: The utility gap of 15.2 comes almost entirely from road sanctions, not from deliveries. C delivers the most on time (about 28.4 on-time, rate 0.99) but carries 18.2 of the town's 20.0 sanction points, which leaves its utility at 10.2 against 25.2 for A and 25.4 for B. The sanctions come from 19.0 release overstays (Minor, 0.5 each, about 9.5) and 7.0 blocking_guard evictions (Major, 1.5 each, about 10.5). The evictions are tied to D1's block_k 2, and C, which parks on the road, bears most of both. Service is healthy with low orders: on-time rate 0.98, worst company 0.96, no unfinished orders. So the levers that matter for this KPI are the road rules that generate sanctions, but A, which never waits on the road, absorbs the most blocked time (556 s).

proposals.title: Re-measure D1: block_k 2 → 3
proposals.rationale: K5 asked for D1 to be re-measured under the new KPI. blocking_guard evictions (7.0 per period, about 10.5 sanction points) fall mostly on C, and raising block_k back to 3 should cut those Major sanctions and narrow utility_gap from 15.2 toward roughly 6–8. D1 relied on rush-volume gains in on-time deliveries and p95 wait; in the quiet season (120 s order interval) congestion is lower, so on_time_rate and min_company_on_time_rate should change little, though blocked_s may rise, mostly for A. Expected votes: C yes and B likely yes, giving a quorum; A likely no because it is the company most blocked. The objective gate (on_time_deliveries +1.0) may not be met.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 3 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
proposals.why_human: This reverses D1, a human decision adopted against the vote, and the human explicitly asked for it to be re-measured. The trade-off is C's sanctions against A's blocked time (556 s already). That is a fairness judgment between companies, and the on-time objective gate does not capture it.

proposals.title: Lengthen hold_limit 60 s → 70 s
proposals.rationale: Release overstays are the largest single violation source (19.0 per period, about 9.5 sanction points), and they fall mostly on C, which waits on the road. A 10 s longer hold limit should convert part of these into compliant holds, lowering sanction_total and utility_gap with little effect on on_time_rate in the quiet season. Risk: longer holds may add blocked seconds, mostly for A, and possibly trigger more blocking_guard evictions. Expected votes: C and B yes (both have road sanctions), A neutral to no; the on-time objective gain may be under +1.0.

proposals.title: Lower sanction_lambda 0.5 → 0.0
proposals.rationale: Sanctions (20.0 total, 18.2 on C) are essentially the whole utility_gap. Setting lambda to 0 would make utility equal to on-time deliveries (about A 25.2, B 27.2, C 28.4), so the gap would fall from 15.2 to about 3 without changing delivery behavior directly. The risk is Goodhart: with no penalty, road holding and blocking may grow, which raises A's blocked time and could lower on_time_rate. The violations are still recorded, so this would be visible. Expected votes: B and C yes, and A yes, since its utility does not fall; the on-time objective gate is unlikely to show +1.0.

proposals.why_human: Removing sanctions narrows the measured utility_gap by switching off the measurement of road misuse, not by changing who uses the road unfairly. A, which never parks on the road, would keep absorbing blocked time with no compensation. Whether that counts as 'no company gains or loses because of how the road is used' is a value judgment for the human, not something the metric can settle.
